answer.rationale: Memory c2 shows the low-cost vendor has a track record of quick onboarding, accurate invoicing, and sharp unit cost reduction — directly relevant to meeting the 18% spend mandate. Memory c6 confirms that longer-term commitments with the incumbent already unlocked volume pricing, but the incumbent has now refused to reopen price this cycle, so the incumbent path is exhausted. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so inaction is not an option. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the finance mandate alone, and c2's evidence of reliable past performance keeps delivery risk bounded. The 94% line utilization with no buffer is the main risk; I would mitigate by structuring the switch with a short overlap window on the incumbent's final delivery cycle if operationally feasible, and by confirming the low-cost vendor's lead time covers the 14-day gap before formal cutover. Adding a second source (c3) or deferring (c5) would be preferable under normal conditions, but the 14-day hard deadline and single-decision capacity make them infeasible this cycle.
